verified: Checked 2026-09-25 against the documents themselves. partI, immediateNote, antecedentNote, partII, interval, mannerQuestion, injuryQuestion, manner, maternalQuestion, maternal, deliveryQuestion and deliveryOptions are the printed wording of ORGI Form No. 4 (the form prints 'as a consequences of'; the Physicians' Manual section 2.3.3 and WHO use 'as a consequence of', used here). Form No. 4 has three Part I lines, (a) to (c); the Manual (2.3.3) allows extra lines when the sequence has more than three stages. Form No. 4A has the same Part I, Part II and pregnancy questions but no manner of death question. modesOfDying: 'heart failure' and 'asthenia' from Form No. 4 and the Manual (1.3); 'respiratory failure' from the Manual (2.3.3) and Form 4 directions; 'cardiac arrest' from WHO 2015; the rest from the ICMR-NCDIR 2022 audit framework list of mechanisms of death that must not be written in Part I (cardio respiratory arrest, cardio respiratory failure, renal or kidney failure, shock, respiratory failure or arrest, heart failure, syncope, multi organ or system failure, asthenia or exhaustion, coma or brain failure); spacing variants of the same terms are included for matching. The ICMR list also pairs 'heart attack' with cardiac arrest; it is left out because myocardial infarction is a valid cause when stated specifically. vagueTerms: 'old age' and 'senility' from Form 4 directions and the Manual (2.6.3 item 19: not to be given if a more specific cause is known, Part II only if contributory); convulsions, diarrhoea, ascites, jaundice and debility from the Form 4 'symptomatic statement' direction ('fever', also listed there, is left out because the helper's substring check would then flag specific diseases such as dengue fever and enteric fever); 'natural death', 'unconscious' and 'cva' from the ICMR-NCDIR 2022 framework. maternalAge (15 to 49 years) from the Manual 2.5. medicoLegalNote from the Manual 1.4 and 2.4. tips from Form 4 directions, the Manual 2.3.2 to 2.3.5 and WHO 2015. The Manual text was read from the Tamil Nadu CRS copy at www.crstn.org because the censusindia.gov.in copy failed TLS verification.
partI: (b) Due to (or as a consequence of)
(c) Due to (or as a consequence of)
immediateNote: State the disease, injury or complication which caused death, not the mode of dying such as heart failure, asthenia, etc.
antecedentNote: Morbid conditions, if any, giving rise to the above cause, stating underlying conditions last
partII: Other significant conditions contributing to the death but not related to the disease or condition causing it
interval: Interval between onset and death approx.
maternalQuestion: If deceased was a female, was pregnancy the death associated with?
deliveryQuestion: If yes, was there a delivery?
medicoLegalNote: In violent deaths and other medico-legal cases the certificate may be completed by the medical examiner at the post-mortem stage; the hospital informs the Registrar of the fact of death.
tips: One condition per line, with disease names written in full and no abbreviations.
Line (a) is the disease, injury or complication that directly caused death, never a mode of dying such as heart failure, respiratory failure or cardiac arrest.
Each line is due to the condition on the line below it; the underlying cause, which started the sequence, goes on the lowest used line of Part I.
Give the approximate interval between onset and death for every condition, e.g. from birth, several years or unknown.
Part II holds other conditions that contributed but were not part of the sequence. Old age or senility goes only in Part II, and never when a more specific cause is known.
For injury or poisoning, state the nature of the injury and the external cause; if accident, suicide or homicide is not yet known, still fill in the cause and mark the manner Pending investigation.
